gloss: I, you, he, she, we, they
title: saya, kamu, dia… — pronouns
pattern: saya / aku · Bapak / Ibu / kamu · dia · kami / kita · mereka
explanation: Saya is the polite 'I', for anyone you don't know well, and aku the casual one, for friends, a partner and children. For 'you', use kamu with friends and people younger than you; with anyone older or a stranger, say Bapak (Pak) to a man and Ibu (Bu) to a woman, or use their name: Bapak mau ke mana? (Where are you going?). Dia is both 'he' and 'she', and mereka is 'they'. 'We' has two words: kita includes the person you're talking to, and kami leaves them out.
natural: Saya is never wrong, so it's the safe choice. Bapak and Ibu aren't only for the old: anyone a bit older than you, or in a role like shopkeeper, driver or official, gets one. Kita is the friendly 'we' that brings your listener in: Kita makan di mana? (Where shall we eat?)
stiff: Kamu to an older person or a stranger sounds rude, and Anda, though polite, sounds stiff face to face: it's the 'you' of signs, forms and adverts. Keep the pairs together: aku goes with kamu, and saya with Bapak and Ibu.

gap.why: To an older man, Bapak is the polite 'you'; kamu is too familiar and Anda too stiff.
A 'we' that includes the person you're asking is kita.
Your listener isn't the boy's parent, so 'our' leaves them out: kami.
Aku and kamu go together, between friends; Anda doesn't match aku, and dia is he or she.
